claude_code.supported_min_source: the .claude-plugin/marketplace.json schema this catalog ships has been stable since 2.0.0; the previous floor was never validated
claude_code.verification_method: Real direct CLI check this run — `claude --version` on the runner reports `2.1.268 (Claude Code)`, continuing the run of live-CLI validation since 2.1.257. `validated_against` and `latest_known` both advance from 2.1.263 to **2.1.268** together (no divergence), covering the 2.1.264 → 2.1.268 delta. Three items from 2.1.268 are directly relevant and documented: **`--json` added to `claude plugin install/uninstall/update/enable/disable`, and `errorDetails`/`noteDetails` added to each `claude plugin list --json` row** — noted in the install guide's Useful-flags section and a new Troubleshooting row, since a contributor scripting a catalog-install smoke test (or diagnosing a broken install) can now get structured output/diagnostics from every plugin lifecycle subcommand instead of only `plugin validate`; **`/plugin` install/enable/disable now take effect on menu close with no `/reload-plugins` needed** — extends the existing 2.1.221 instant-activation note (previously install-only) to enable/disable too, documented alongside it; and **plugin/marketplace error messages no longer leak a token or password embedded in a git source URL** — noted in `docs/agent-guidelines/security.md` as a defense-in-depth confirmation (this catalog's own entries use the credential-free `github`+`repo` shorthand, never a URL with embedded credentials, so it was never exposed either way, but the guidance now says so explicitly for contributors who test a URL-form source locally). Reviewed and not applicable, checked directly rather than assumed: `claude plugin validate` rejecting a plugin path whose directory name begins with two dots (2.1.268 fix) — this catalog's entries are always `github` sources, never local directories, so no plugin path here can begin with dots; a default monitors file or root `SKILL.md` silently skipped when it can't be checked (2.1.268 fix) — re-ran `claude plugin validate --strict --json .agents/skills` live against the 2.1.268 CLI and it reports `"success": true` with an empty `contents` array, so this catalog's root `SKILL.md` was already being checked cleanly either way; the Claude apps gateway `pricing:`/`gatewayInternalNetworks` additions and `claude self-hosted-runner --remove-session-state` (all 2.1.268) — this is a personal catalog with no gateway or self-hosted runner configured; and `configDirectory` added to `claude auth status --json` (2.1.268) — no script here calls `claude auth status`. 2.1.264 and 2.1.266 shipped no itemized changelog entries beyond bug fixes/reliability improvements, and 2.1.267's own two items (the Discover/Browse missing-description fix and marketplace-description-authority change) plus its marketplace-entry-backslash-containment security fix — reviewed, nothing further to adopt beyond what was already documented for those. Everything else in 2.1.264–2.1.268 is host/session/UI-side with zero marketplace-manifest, plugin-source, or skill-loading surface. `claude plugin validate --strict --json .agents/skills` (piped through `scripts/report-skill-validation.py`) and a full `make validate` (regenerate + validate manifests, `make agent:check`; 3 plugins in sync, no drift) both passed clean against the live 2.1.268 CLI. Prior 2.1.252→2.1.263 verification still holds unchanged; see the install guide's per-version sections for that full history. Catalog install previously verified with `claude plugin marketplace add Tamircohen28/tamirs-marketplace` followed by `claude plugin install <name>@tamirs-marketplace`.

cursor.supported_min_source: Cursor documents no minimum version for plugins; the floor is the version actually validated rather than guessed. The previous 0.45.0 floor predates Cursor's plugin system entirely
cursor.verification_method: latest desktop build from official Cursor download links (3.18.9, 2026-08-30 stable) cross-checked against cursor.com/changelog (feature 3.11; date-only entries through 2026-09-02 Self-Hosted Machines / Team Pools / partner sandboxes / computer use); team-marketplace import is a Dashboard flow

codex.supported_min_source: earliest release this catalog has claimed .agents/plugins/marketplace.json support for
codex.verification_method: documentary revalidation by this repo's standing Codex method (official release notes plus catalog compatibility review; the Codex CLI is not installed on the review machine). Reviewed every openai/codex release from 0.148.0 through 0.153.4 for plugin/marketplace changes: #41208 (0.151.0) reports invalid project marketplaces without hiding valid plugins, #41953 (0.153.0) enforces a marketplace source policy for OpenAI-curated plugins only, and #42149/#42150 (0.153.0) upgrade Git marketplaces from merged configuration and add remote-marketplace support to the plugin CLI. None alter the portable Agent Plugin catalog shape, so .agents/plugins/marketplace.json remains discoverable unchanged; 0.153.0 widens how it can be consumed rather than narrowing it.

opencode.supported_min_source: oldest version on which `skills.paths` discovery of a catalog plugin's skills was verified with `opencode debug skill`
opencode.verification_method: `opencode --version` on the maintainer machine (reported 1.18.29); latest from registry.npmjs.org/opencode-ai. OpenCode has no marketplace, so the catalog itself cannot be installed — skill discovery is verified directly with `opencode debug skill`, pointing `skills.paths` at this repo's `.agents/skills` and confirming `run-plugins-catalog` resolves to its `SKILL.md`

capability_gaps.marketplace: OpenCode has no plugin marketplace and no plugin manifest, so this catalog cannot be added as an install source. Each plugin repo is installed directly — clone it and point `skills.paths` at its `skills/` directory, or symlink it into the OpenCode skills directory. Every plugin in this catalog ships its own `opencode.json` and its own OpenCode install guide.
capability_gaps.catalog_discovery: There is no OpenCode equivalent of listing plugins from a remote catalog. The plugin table in this repo's README is the discovery surface; installation is then per-repo.
